name: type7_filmtest_2D_L340um_eps0.86um
comment: Type 7 film-persistence test (user, 2026-11-13: 'if we are going to apply these films, we should have some tests for it'). A 340 um segment of rough wall with pore A' wall statistics (bump half-width 40-60 um, height 0.5-0.7 of the half-width, overlap 0.25-0.4, smoothed with sigma 8 um; ASSUMED grain size, no source), mean gap 120 um, no throat. Ice: a 6.0 um (7 eps) rind along the whole bottom wall (it meets both pore ends, where the 90-degree phi face makes it a film with no ends), an 8.6 um (10 eps) rind on the top wall over x 80-230 um (round ends), and one contact neck (R 21.5 um, 25 eps) in the top-wall valley at x = 292 um. theta = 60 deg (D1, an assumption). Expected under closed isothermal vapor: the films are not stable in this model (curvature only, no disjoining pressure or crystallographic term); they should thin on grain tips and thicken into valleys, the ends of the top rind retract, and ice collect in the valleys and the neck. Mesh: "ny_rule": "bbox" sizes Ny from the bounding height so the solver's start-up resolution check (Ly/Ny) passes (finer across the pore than the type-7 default).
